claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'd like to claim for my child Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I have a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This usually means the child lives with you, or you're contributing to the cost of looking after them at a rate of at least the same amount as Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm responsible for Alex. He lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that Alex lives with you.

**Does Alex live in the UK?** And are you also living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me here in the UK. We live in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex still in full-time education or training, and has this been the case continuously since they turned 16?** (Since Alex is 8, this wouldn't apply yet, but I want to confirm there are no unusual circumstances.)

Actually, given Alex is only 8 years old, that question isn't relevant yet. Let me ask instead:

**Are there any other circumstances I should know about regarding Alex, such as:**
- Is Alex in hospital or local authority care?
- Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
- Have you recently moved to the UK from another country?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex has been in care for a couple of months now, but he comes home to stay with me most of the time - he's here quite a lot during the week and on weekends.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex being in care. This is important for assessing your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me, Alex has been in local authority care for a couple of months (more than 8 weeks), but he comes home to stay with you regularly.

To confirm your eligibility, I need to clarify:

**When Alex comes home to stay with you, does he typically spend either:**
- **At least 2 nights in a row each week with you**, OR
- **7 days or more in a row at home with you at any time?**

This is important because the rules allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit for a child in care if they meet one of these conditions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's home with me quite a bit - he stays at least a couple of nights every week with me, sometimes more.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's very helpful.

Just one more question to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** For example, another family member or the local authority?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Alex is under 16** (he's 8 years old)
✅ **You live in the UK** (Manchester)
✅ **You are responsible for Alex**
✅ **No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him**

Regarding Alex being in care: Although he has been in local authority care for more than 8 weeks, you still qualify because **Alex spends at least 2 nights in a row each week at home with you**. This meets the exception rule that allows you to continue receiving Child Benefit for a child in care.

**Important:** You should inform HMRC about Alex's care situation if you haven't already, so they have accurate records. You can do this by filling in an online form or contacting HMRC by phone or post.

If you have any other questions, please feel free to ask!
